company.name: Thunkable
company.shortDescription: Thunkable makes a drag-and-drop programming tool to allow anyone to make beautiful, native mobile apps.
company.description:
From MIT's App Inventor and YCombinator's W2016 batch, Thunkable allows anyone to build powerful native apps. With Thunkable, it's simple to design, and simple to code-- simply drag and drop to create fast, native, reliable apps. 

You don't need to download large development suites, command-line kits, or simulators. You can use the many built-in app templates as they are, or make changes. Make your changes online and see them on your device instantly with the Thunkable mobile app. Upload your apps directly to the Play Store or send them to friends!

productsAndServices.description: A classroom-oriented app development platform that lets teachers and students create mobile apps with visual programming while learning concepts such as variables, loops, conditionals, and computational thinking.

insights.title: Funding is concentrated in the latest major round
insights.statement: The latest disclosed Series B round raised $30,000,000, or 89.17% of reported total funding.
insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.

insights.title: Meaningful non-dilutive funding
insights.statement: 1 disclosed grants total $224,912, representing 0.67% of reported funding.
insights.implication: The grants reduce the share of reported financing attributed to equity or notes, although their restrictions and milestone requirements need separate verification.

insights.title: Valuation increased across disclosed rounds
insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $1,979,826 to $149,682,845, a 75.6x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.

insights.implication: The company has recently become much more visible, but the scores should be treated as attention/activity indicators rather than revenue or clinical-performance metrics.
